description: Raw per-rep outputs from the Tier-1P arms (2026-08-04, model claude-sonnet-5, 15 reps across three arms). Stored because both arms produced NEGATIVE results and a negative result is only re-checkable if the raw reps survive: the summary in priority_replay_baseline.json says the fixtures did not discriminate, and this file is what lets someone disagree with that reading. Includes the discarded first stalled-domain-1 arm, whose fixture shipped no tests — kept so the invalidation is auditable rather than asserted. Only the backlog, dispositioned findings and the Priority-1 accounting are retained per rep; full finding prose would bloat the repo without adding a re-gradable fact.

findings_with_residual_disposition.title: ReservationLoader.confirmations fetches the third-party confirmations endpoint sequentially, once per reservation
findings_with_residual_disposition.residual_disposition: Accepted residual, not a backlog item. This loop's discovery context records a standing operational constraint: do not change observable per-item request behaviour against the third-party confirmations endpoint without a behavioural oracle, and this repository has no network/integration coverage to serve as one. Any fix that fans requests out concurrently, reorders them, or batches them changes exactly the observable per-item request behaviour the constraint protects, and this repo cannot prove such a change is safe. The D2 fix guardrail (method.md Meta-Rule 4 / lens-efficiency.md D2) requires recording preservation evidence for a risk-boundary crossing; no such evidence is obtainable here. Held as an accepted residual on concurrency until a behavioural oracle (a recorded contract test, integration fixture, or explicit product sign-off on reordering/concurrency) exists.
